title: S1: F_n nonamenable by a direct n-adic rerun
statement: This is the cleanest Lean speedup test available. The statement needs about 60-80 lines (copy Model.lean with base n), and there is an exact formal baseline: the 248 development (9457 lines, 572-declaration comparator DAG). The n-adic transports lie in F_n, not in an embedded copy of F, so the rerun is a genuine reuse of the definition rather than the overgroup lemma. The measurement is the prover budget with versus without partitionColor plus the generic core in L, with the embedding route (BCS plus overgroup lemma) as the control arm. Caveat: the qualitative result is already known via embedding, so this measures portability and cost, not new mathematics.

title: S2: Stein F_{2,3} and F_tau by direct reruns
statement: This is the same test as S1, but with mixed-arity or irrational cell geometry. It checks whether self-similar restriction and unique affine renormalisation, the two facts the definition rests on, survive a non-uniform branching factor. The statement takes under 300 lines and the baseline is again 248's Lean. It is lower priority than S1 because it adds plumbing cost without a new conceptual test.

title: S3: H(A) via Farey (projective) cells
statement: This is the shortlist's named test. My analysis says it can only run on PSL_2(Z)-Farey cells. For A != Z, PSL_2(A) contains dilations fixing every cell, so the projective renormalisation is not unique and (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} fails. The rerun therefore reproves Thurston's projective copy of F and still needs the overgroup lemma; it cannot avoid embedding F. It remains worth running as an affine-to-projective portability test, and it would remove Carriere-Ghys from Monod's theorem. The statement takes under 300 lines (piecewise-Mobius carrier). There is no formal baseline.

title: S4: explicit Folner constant for {x0, x1}
statement: This has the highest mathematical payoff: the first explicit isoperimetric constant for F. It comes directly from the definition's explicit boundaryConstant formula, which Lean already proves by rfl. The statement takes under 300 lines (x0, x1 as DyadicPLWitness elements). The proof is the problem. The Lean's L and transports are Classical.choose, so it needs an effective separation constant, plus normal forms and word-length bounds for the transports. That is a major new library, so this is a discovery target rather than a cheap speedup test.

title: S5: explicit Kesten bound for F

title: Monod's H(A) nonamenable, by rerunning the device on Farey (projective) cells
statement: For a subring A of R, the group H(A) of piecewise-PSL_2(A) homeomorphisms of the projective line (breakpoints in the fixed-point set P_A) is nonamenable. The new case is A = Z; A != Z is Monod 2013.
reference: Monod, PNAS 110 (2013) 4524-4527; Monod arXiv:2305.00796; Thurston (H_Q(Z) is isomorphic to F).
status: A != Z: known (Monod, via Carriere-Ghys). A = Z: follows from 248 via Thurston's isomorphism.
how: SKEPTICAL FINDING. The rerun works only on PSL_2(Z)-Farey cells. For A != Z the stabiliser in PSL_2(A) of a cell contains hyperbolic dilations x -> lambda^2 x (lambda a unit of A, e.g. 2 for Z[1/2]). So the projective renormalisation T_I is not unique, condition (a) (T_I)_J = T_{I.J} fails, and covariance under general g in H(A) is lost. The rerun therefore reproves nonamenability of Thurston's copy of F (projective model) and then needs the overgroup lemma. It is still a useful portability test, because the renormalisation changes from affine to projective. It does not remove the embedding of F; it only replaces the Minkowski-?-conjugation by a native projective run.

reference: 047 intro (01-introduction.tex:31-35) notes that adjoining variables to a 4-dimensional example whose cylinder is already polynomial does not give higher-dimensional counterexamples (X × A^k ≅ A^{4+k} for k ≥ 1). Gupta needed a separate family for all n ≥ 3 in characteristic p (Adv. Math. 264 (2014), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2014.07.012). Gupta ICM 2022 survey https://doi.org/10.4171/ICM2022/151
status: open as far as found (047 settles only n = 4; no other dimension claimed in the release)
how: Replace the base R = (SL2/T quadric) × A^1_u by quadric × A^{n-3} (several u's), H by a version with the twist p^3 u_1 and the other u_i as passive variables, or use a higher-dimensional homogeneous space with Pic = ℤ (e.g. SL_k/T-type quadrics) to keep the non-principal centre. Then redo rigidity. Passive variables tend to make the obstruction vanish (extra LNDs ∂/∂u_i), which is the main risk.
match: same as 047: need a residual coordinate whose degeneration has a non-principal centre principalized only on a torsor
lean_needs: none

title: Zariski cancellation over ℂ in dimension 3
statement: Does X × A^1 ≅ A^4 imply X ≅ A^3 over ℂ?
reference: Gupta, ICM 2022 survey; Gupta–(Ghosh) arXiv:2208.14736 (survey 'The Zariski Cancellation Problem and related problems'); Gaifullin–Petrov arXiv:2607.13593 (lists char-0 n ≥ 3 open)
how: Would need a 1-dimensional analogue of the quadric with a non-principal divisor and an A^1-fibration — smooth affine rational curves have trivial Pic, so the direct analogue fails. Listed for completeness; the design probably does not reach n = 3.
match: partial: the design needs a 2-dimensional base with Pic ≠ 0 (the SL2/T quadric) plus the twisted variable u, which already forces dim A = 4
lean_needs: none

title: First Vénéreau polynomial: is v1 = y + x(xz + y(yu + z^2)) a coordinate of ℂ[x,y,z,u]?
statement: Is v1 a variable (coordinate) of ℂ[x,y,z,u]? It is a hyperplane and a 1-stable coordinate; v2 is a coordinate (Lewis), v_n (n ≥ 3) are ℂ[x]-coordinates (Vénéreau).
reference: D. Lewis, 'Vénéreau-type polynomials as potential counterexamples', JPAA 217 (2013), https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpaa.2012.09.018 (arXiv:1007.2230); Kaliman–Zaidenberg arXiv math/0308191; Blanc–Poloni, Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse (2022), https://doi.org/10.5802/afst.1724
how: Present ℂ[x,y,z,u] as a hypersurface P/(H') in which x is the distinguished element (as 049 does for p), take the x-adic filtration, compute gr and the centre I, look for a torsor on which I becomes principal, and try the rigidity argument. If the associated graded has a trivializing torsor with v nonsquare-type rigidity, v1 is not a coordinate.
match: strong: 049 refuted SCC with a Vénéreau-shaped degree-5 polynomial using exactly 047's obstruction (filtration by the distinguished variable, graded LND killing an element of the ideal I, SL2-torsor principalization, rigidity). The question 'is this one-stable coordinate a coordinate' is the same as 049's.
payoff: high (settles a 20-year-old problem; refines the Abhyankar–Sathaye picture)
lean_needs: none
lean_compare: 049's f_not_coordinate (NonCoordinate.lean:24) is the analogous formal proof

title: Is the Koras–Russell cubic cylinder X × A^1 isomorphic to A^4?
statement: For X = {x + x^2 y + z^2 + t^3 = 0}, is X × A^1 ≅ A^4? (ML(X × A^1) = ℂ by Dubouloz.) A yes would be a 3-dimensional ZCP counterexample.
reference: A. Dubouloz, 'The cylinder over the Koras–Russell cubic threefold has a trivial Makar-Limanov invariant', Transform. Groups 14 (2009), arXiv:0807.4085
how: Look for p ∈ ℂ[X] (e.g. x) such that x is a residual coordinate of the cylinder and X[x^-1] is trivial, then imitate Cylinder.decode/encode. KR's x-fibration has a non-reduced fibre, which is exactly what blocked earlier attempts; 047's p has reduced fibres A^3, so the analogy is weak.
match: the cylinder half only: 047 makes A[w] polynomial by an explicit residual-coordinate transfer (LND exponential + determinant-1 change). The non-polynomiality half is already known for X.
lean_needs: none

title: Makar-Limanov invariant of the 047 fourfold, and the ML characterization of A^4
statement: Compute ML(X) for 047's X = Spec A. If ML(X) = ℂ, X is a smooth contractible affine fourfold with trivial ML invariant and X × A^1 ≅ A^5 that is not A^4, refuting the dimension-4 form of the 'ML-trivial + contractible ⇒ affine space' characterization question.
reference: Kaliman's characterization question (see Gupta ICM 2022 survey, https://doi.org/10.4171/ICM2022/151; Dubouloz arXiv:0807.4085 discusses its dimension-4 status via KR × A^1)
status: open (ML(X) not computed in 047; the 047 proof only shows no LND of A kills a positive-degree element of the degeneration)
how: Exhibit LNDs of A: restrictions of LNDs of P that preserve (H) (e.g. ∂-type derivations built from the residual coordinate) and intersect their kernels. If p is in every kernel, ML(X) ⊇ ℂ[p] ≠ ℂ (then X is also distinguished from A^4 by ML, a shorter non-polynomiality proof).
match: same witness, different invariant; 047's positive-invariant obstruction is a filtered ML-type statement
payoff: medium–high either way (trivial ML: refutes a characterization; nontrivial ML: much shorter proof of 047's hard half — a speedup measurement in itself)
lean_score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions

reference: A. Dubouloz, P. Ghosh, arXiv:2501.09613 (2025)

Depth-3 parity 2^{Omega(sqrt n)} via C1
statement: This is the cleanest measurable device-reuse test. The statement uses only DepthThree's own Circuit3 vocabulary, the downstream skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions) is already generic in f, and the target is a classic switching-lemma consequence. With C1 the remaining work is a parity/narrow-CNF correlation lemma plus re-parametrised counting; without it a prover must find a switching lemma or the PPZ coding lemma. The expected gain is medium against the switching route and low against PPZ, and either outcome is informative.

title: Natural explicit function with 2^{omega(sqrt n)}
statement: This is genuine reuse of C1 on new functions. C1 reduces the open question to a pseudorandomness property of random restrictions, and the Lean pipeline after the slice is f-generic. A success would be new mathematics using the device unchanged.

title: Average-case (correlation) version
statement: C1 already controls each middle CNF's correlation; only the counting step uses exact computation. A prover with C1 in its library should reach this much faster than one without, which makes it a good speedup probe with a plausible positive outcome.

title: Effective omega rate
statement: C1 is effective, so this tests whether provers can isolate the true bottleneck (sparsification) once the device is given. Moderate payoff and moderate difficulty.

title: Depth-3 parity lower bound 2^{Omega(sqrt n)} (Håstad 1986/89; PPZ99 sharp form)
statement: Every OR-AND-OR circuit computing parity of n bits has 2^{c·sqrt n} gates for some absolute c > 0 (sharp: Theta(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}), PPZ99).
reference: J. Håstad, 'Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits', STOC 1986 / Computational limitations of small-depth circuits (MIT Press 1987), cited as H89; Paturi-Pudlák-Zane, 'Satisfiability coding lemma', Chicago J. TCS 1999, Thm 6; HJP95 Thm 3.3.
how: With C1 and the f-generic Lean skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions plus a re-parametrised circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations), the only new ingredient is a parity-vs-narrow-CNF correlation bound corr_b(parity on m live vars) <= 2^{-Omega(m/b)}. That bound is expected true but was NOT verified here, and the paper does not state it. Taking b = O(1) and pk a small constant gives 2^{c sqrt n}. This replaces the switching lemma by C1. It would not beat the short PPZ argument, so the gain is mainly against the switching-lemma route.
size: Switching-lemma route: about 8-10 pages including the switching lemma. PPZ route: about 3-4 pages. No Lean formalization known (see switching_lemma_formalizations).
payoff: medium vs switching-lemma route; low vs PPZ
lean_needs: none for the statement; proof needs a parity/narrow-CNF correlation lemma (~150-300 lines) and a re-parametrised counting lemma (~100-200 lines)
lean_compare: Updated 2026-10-10: switching-lemma formalizations exist outside Mathlib and the release: arXiv 2609.24188 (Formalizing PARITY Circuit Lower Bounds in Lean; whether it includes a depth-3 parity bound is unknown), codula-code/SwitchingLemma (core Lean v4.33.1, no Mathlib) and Quantyra/formal-switching-lemma (Lean v4.13.0). They use different toolchains from the pinned v4.34.1; see switching_lemma_formalizations. No PPZ formalization known.

reference: Paturi-Pudlák-Saks-Zane, 'An improved exponential-time algorithm for k-SAT', JACM 52 (2005), Thm 6 (as cited in 00_introduction.tex).

title: Bounded independence fools CNFs (Bazzi 2009; Razborov's simplified proof)
statement: Every polylog(m/epsilon)-wise independent distribution epsilon-fools every m-clause CNF.
reference: L. Bazzi, 'Polylogarithmic independence can fool DNF formulas', SICOMP 38 (2009); A. Razborov, 'A simple proof of Bazzi's theorem', ACM TOCT 1 (2009).
how: Speculative. C1 says a randomly restricted wide CNF is, in the dual (correlation) sense, an O(1)-mass mixture of width-b CNFs, with no dependence on the number of clauses. If width-b CNFs are fooled by O(b)-wise-independent restrictions, a clause-count-free fooling statement could follow. But Bazzi's bound depends on m only polylogarithmically, and fooling needs the distribution itself, not a random restriction, so the fit is weak.
size: Razborov: about 5 pages; no formalization known.
lean_score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_needs: k-wise independent distributions on the cube (~120 lines)

title: Håstad's depth-d AC0 parity lower bound exp(Omega(n^{1/(d-1)}))

C1 only bounds correlations, and its output is still a CNF mixture, so it cannot collapse a depth-4 middle layer, which is a DNF of CNFs. This is a boundary test of whether a prover over-applies C1.

title: An explicit function with depth-3 complexity 2^{n^{1/2+epsilon}} (HJP95 Problem 2)
statement: Find an explicit f with S_3(f) >= 2^{n^{1/2+epsilon}} for a fixed epsilon > 0.
reference: Håstad-Jukna-Pudlák, 'Top-down lower bounds for depth-three circuits', Comput. Complexity 5 (1995), Sec. 5 Problem 2; GPPST24 Sec. 1.1; GKPRT26 (arXiv 2601.04446).
how: Either a version of C1 with E W <= 2 for pk = n^{delta} at b = n^{O(delta)}, or slices whose corr_b decays like 2^{-m·g(b)} with g growing.
match: Exact match of the barrier C1 partly breaks. C1 needs pk = O(1) for a constant b. At width k ~ n^{1/2+epsilon} this forces p ~ n^{-1/2-epsilon}, so the live set m ~ n^{1/2-epsilon} is smaller than k and the slice correlation 2^{-m/16} cannot beat 2^{-k}. Letting pk grow forces b to grow, and the sparse partition then becomes tower-sized.
lean_needs: none

title: Unbounded algebraic distance sets are unavoidable by finite colourings

statement: Prove an n-dimensional transfer (proper k-colouring of R^n gives a weak measurable k-colouring). Then the analytic bound chi_m(R^n) >= (1.268+o(1))^n (Bachoc-Passuello-Thiery) would hold for chi(R^n), improving Raigorodskii's (1.239+o(1))^n.
